article_content: A 42-year-old woman from Rochester, Kent, died on December 9 at King's College Hospital in London after injecting heroin contaminated with anthrax. Claire Skelton's death was due to anthrax and intravenous drug abuse. This is the third death in Britain linked to an anthrax outbreak among drug users. The Health Protection Agency reported 13 anthrax cases among drug users across Europe since June. Six cases were in the UK: four in England, one in Scotland, and one in Wales. Anthrax can be treated with antibiotics if diagnosed early. Dr Fortune Ncube stressed that medical professionals should watch for anthrax symptoms in drug users. These symptoms include severe infections, blood poisoning, high fever, chills, and breathing difficulties.

Claire Skelton'ın ölümü antraks ve damar içi uyuşturucu kullanımına bağlandı. Bu, Britanya'da uyuşturucu kullanıcıları arasında görülen antraks salgınına bağlı üçüncü ölüm. Sağlık Koruma Ajansı, Haziran'dan bu yana Avrupa genelinde uyuşturucu kullananlar arasında 13 antraks vakası bildirdi. Bu vakaların altısı İngiltere'deydi; dördü İngiltere, biri İskoçya ve biri Galler'deydi. Antraks, erken teşhis edilirse antibiyotiklerle tedavi edilebilir. Dr Fortune Ncube, sağlık çalışanlarının uyuşturucu kullanıcılarında antraks belirtilerini dikkatle izlemesi gerektiğini vurguladı. Bu belirtiler arasında şiddetli enfeksiyonlar, kan zehirlenmesi, yüksek ateş, titreme ve nefes alma zorluğu bulunuyor.

article_content: The number of Americans living in poor neighborhoods has skyrocketed in the last decade, particularly in the South, where over 30% of the population is concentrated in areas with high poverty rates. A new report from the U.S. Census Bureau reveals a solid band of high-poverty neighborhoods stretching from Arizona east to North Carolina, sparing only Florida and Virginia from this trend. The data indicate that poverty in the United States isn't just growing; it's becoming more concentrated, which can worsen social problems and lower social mobility chances. The Census report notes that the number of people living below the federal poverty line - less than '$24,000' a year for a family of four - has increased between 2000 and 2010. The number of Americans living in poverty rose by 45% to 45 million. North Carolina and Tennessee saw the biggest increase in residents living in poor neighborhoods, while Louisiana, West Virginia, Hawaii, and Alaska were the only states where the figure decreased. The number of Americans living in 'poverty areas' - neighborhoods with over 20% impoverished residents - has increased more dramatically. A quarter of the U.S. population, 77 million Americans, lived in poverty areas in 2010, a 56% jump from the 2000 census. In the South, the trend is even more dramatic, with nearly 31% of Southerners living in poor neighborhoods, a 62% increase from 2000.

ABD Sayım Bürosu'ndan yeni bir rapor, Arizona'dan Kuzey Carolina'ya kadar uzanan yüksek yoksulluk oranlarına sahip mahallelerin varlığını ortaya koyuyor. Bu trendden sadece Florida ve Virginia etkilenmedi. 'Yoksulluk alanlarında' yaşayan Amerikalıların sayısı daha da arttı. article_content: Imagine stepping back into the Nineties by watching 'Friends', a time before smartphones and selfie sticks. A new video by 'Nerdist' reimagines this classic sitcom in today's world, with hilarious results. The original characters are replaced by six young adults, dressed in hipster attire, capturing the essence of modern life. In the parody, instead of dancing around a fountain, they focus on their phones, texting, and taking selfies. The iconic theme tune is remixed, addressing modern trends like online dating and vegan diets. The lyrics now include 'your Tinder profile sucks' and 'my battery's really low', highlighting the impact of smartphones on relationships. The modern 'Friends' hang out at 'Woodcat', a hipster cafe, where they continue to stare at their phones, uninterested in each other. The video has been viewed over 350,000 times on YouTube and received comments like 'It's so depressing but so true'.

article_content: Alison Glenn, a 53-year-old from Cambridgeshire, experienced severe jaw pain while dining with friends. She was diagnosed with trigeminal neuralgia, a condition causing extreme facial pain due to nerve damage. Trigeminal neuralgia affects 19,000 people in the UK, primarily those over 50. Alison had four unnecessary root canal treatments before a correct diagnosis was made. Under the care of Professor Joanna Zakrzewska, Alison underwent an MRI scan that confirmed the trigeminal nerve was compressed. Alison had surgery to relieve the compression and has been pain-free since.

Professor Joanna Zakrzewska'nın uzmanlığında Alison'a MRI taraması yapıldı ve trigeminal sinirde baskı olduğu doğrulandı. Alison ameliyat oldu ve o günden beri ağrı hissetmedi.

article_content: Mario Balotelli has decided to drop his appeal against Manchester City's decision to fine him two weeks' wages. The fine was imposed due to Balotelli's poor disciplinary record during the 2011/12 title-winning season. Balotelli, signed from Inter Milan for $39.1 million in 2010, had missed 11 domestic and European games due to suspension. The Italy international's lawyers had prepared to present his case at a Premier League tribunal. Following 'amicable talks', Balotelli chose to accept the fine and withdraw his appeal as a sign of respect for Roberto Mancini, the supporters, and Manchester City. Despite his disciplinary issues, Balotelli played a crucial role in Italy's Euro 2012 campaign and contributed to Manchester City's title win in 2012.

İtalya milliyetçisinin avukatları, Premier Lig tribunali önünde iddialarını sunmaya hazırlanmışlardı. Dostane görüşmelerin ardından Balotelli, Roberto Mancini'ye, taraftarlara ve Manchester City'ye saygı göstergesi olarak para cezasını kabul edip itirazını geri çekmeyi seçti. Disiplin sorunlarına rağmen Balotelli, İtalya'nın Euro 2012 kampanyasında önemli rol oynadı ve Manchester City'nin 2012'deki şampiyonluğuna katkıda bulundu.

article_content: A man who escaped from a minimum security prison in Mississippi 35 years ago and was captured living in Utah has now been returned to Mississippi to serve out the remainder of his sentence, officials said on Friday. Sam Gene Harris, 62, was sentenced in 1979 to six years in prison for burglary and possession of burglary tools. He escaped from the Forrest County Community Work Center in southern Mississippi in 1980. Mississippi authorities learned of Harris's whereabouts from the FBI. Harris was extradited from Utah on Sunday. Before his arrest in January, Harris had lived in Wellington, a town of 1,600 people about 100 miles southeast of Salt Lake City, for 23 years. During his decades on the run, Harris had come into contact with law enforcement and had used aliases. He has lived under at least 10 different names and has escaped from two other jails in Oregon. He also has a criminal history in Florida and Georgia, including charges for theft and assaulting an officer. At the time of his arrest, Harris was living as 'Wayne Stevens' in a small house on a main road. An FBI bulletin about wanted people tipped off Utah police to his identity. Harris tried to convince police they had nabbed the wrong man, however fingerprints proved otherwise. Harris will not incur additional prison time for his escape because fleeing from a community work center was a misdemeanor at the time. He will be eligible for release in 2018.

article_content: At least 905 children have called in sick to schools in a suspected mass food poisoning incident in Japan's Shizuoka Prefecture. This has led the local government to cancel classes at 15 elementary schools to prevent the outbreak from spreading further. The affected children, from Hamamatsu, a city approximately 125 miles southwest of Tokyo, experienced symptoms such as vomiting and diarrhea. Officials reported that 41 teachers and staff members exhibited similar symptoms. Authorities suspect norovirus, a common cause of foodborne illness, to be the probable cause. The virus was 'detected in about half of the stool samples taken from sick pupils,' according to Horihiro Ishizaka, a Hamamatsu city public relations official. The city's hygiene office is currently testing school lunches consumed by the students to confirm the cause of the outbreak. Local news reports indicate that the schools used an ingredient from a shared supplier. In response to the incident, the city has closed most of the affected schools and canceled classes at others through Friday.

Yetkililer, yaygın bir gıda kaynaklı hastalık nedeni olan norovirus'u olası neden olarak şüphelendiler. article_content: A study published in PLOS ONE found that women who have close relationships with their mothers tend to bond better with their babies. Lower levels of the 'love hormone' oxytocin have been found in women who are not close to their mothers. Women with lower oxytocin levels were more likely to experience negative feelings towards their babies, including resentment, depression, and separation anxiety. The findings could help identify at-risk mothers and assist them in developing crucial bonds with their babies, according to UNSW Professor Valsamma Eapen. Professor Eapen and colleagues are developing attachment-based cognitive behavioral therapy to help mothers 'reframe their own perspectives and attitudes.' This therapy could be used alone or with a synthetic version of oxytocin. The study followed 680 pregnant women at Sydney's Liverpool Hospital.

Bulgular, risk altındaki anneleri belirlemeye ve onlara bebekleriyle bağ kurmalarında yardımcı olmaya yardımcı olabilir, diye belirtti UNSW Profesörü Valsamma Eapen. Profesör Eapen ve ekibi, bağlanma temelli bilişsel davranışçı terapi geliştiriyor. Bu terapi, annelerin kendi bakış açılarını yeniden çerçevelemelerine yardımcı olmayı amaçlıyor.

article_content: Dr Mansoor Kassim, a 37-year-old doctor, is facing being struck off the medical register after faking Viagra prescriptions worth £340.67 to the NHS. He did this to address 'marital difficulties' because he was too embarrassed to ask his own GP. Dr Kassim, who worked at Ystrad Fawr Hospital in Caerphilly, South Wales, has already received a suspended jail sentence for his actions. The General Medical Council is now holding a hearing to determine whether his fitness to practise is impaired by his conviction. Dr Kassim told the disciplinary panel that his actions were a 'stupid mistake' made during a 'stressful situation' in his marriage. He expressed remorse and shame, stating that he had been 'very dishonest' and that his actions were inexcusable.

Bunu, kendi doktoruna sormaktan utandığı için 'evlilik zorlukları'nı gidermek için yaptı. Dr Kassim, Güney Galler, Caerphilly'deki Ystrad Fawr Hastanesi'nde çalışıyordu ve eylemleri nedeniyle zaten askıya alınmış bir hapis cezası almıştı. Genel Tıp Konseyi, şimdi onun mesleki yeterliliğinin hüküm giymesinden etkilenip etkilenmediğini belirlemek için bir duruşma düzenliyor. Dr Kassim, disiplin heyetine, eylemlerinin evliliğindeki 'stresli bir durum' sırasında yaptığı 'aptalca bir hata' olduğunu söyledi. Çok pişman olduğunu ve utandığını, 'çok dürüst olmayan' davrandığını ve eylemlerinin mazur görülemeyeceğini belirtti.

Sterilization involves blocking or cutting a woman's Fallopian tubes, making her permanently unable to get pregnant.

article_content: At least four people lost their lives in two days of violent riots in Kampala, Uganda's capital. The unrest was triggered by radio broadcasts in the Buganda Kingdom that incited listeners to cause chaos. Tensions between the Buganda Kingdom and the central government have been escalating over land laws and political power. The rioters damaged police property, vehicles, and shops, and a police station was looted in the Natete-Ndeba suburb. A curfew was declared in the affected areas, and the Ugandan army is supporting the police. More than 50 people were treated for injuries at a local hospital.

Etkilenen bölgelerde sokağa çıkma yasağı uygulandı ve Uganda ordusu polisi destekliyor. Yerel bir hastanede 50'den fazla kişi yaralanma nedeniyle tedavi gördü.

article_content: Former Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak is expected to be brought to Cairo next week for questioning in a corruption case, according to Mustafa Bakri, a former member of parliament. Bakri, who filed the case against Mubarak, was informed of the development by the Prosecutor General's office on Thursday. Attorney General Abdel Maguid Mahmoud issued an order freezing the assets of Mubarak and his family on Monday and prohibited them from leaving the country. Egyptian Prime Minister Ahmed Shafik resigned, and the Egyptian military appointed former transport minister Essam Sharaf as the new Prime Minister. Bakri provided documents indicating Mubarak's family has secret bank accounts totaling more than $147 million. Mubarak has denied allegations of amassing wealth, calling them 'fabrications and baseless rumors'. Bakri claims the documents he provided are 'the first solid and concrete evidence' of Mubarak's illegal fortune.

article_content: Now that Google Drive is a reality, let's compare it to its cloud competition. Google's cloud-based document and storage solution is priced aggressively and integrates well with other Google services, including Google Docs. Google Drive is impressive but faces competition from Box, Dropbox, Apple, Microsoft, and Amazon. Storage and Pricing: Google Drive costs $30/year for 25GB and $60/year for 100GB. This is competitive with Amazon and Microsoft. The upload limit is 10GB, higher than most cloud services. Collaboration and Sharing: Google Drive offers in-browser access to files and folders, including document editing via Google Docs. Mobile Integration: Google Drive has an Android app, but iOS users must wait. Desktop Integration: Google Drive's desktop app works like SkyDrive. Final Thoughts: Choosing a cloud storage service depends on more than specs and pricing. Users should try a service before upgrading.

article_content: More than 4,700 square miles of ice formed over the Great Lakes in one night on Tuesday. The Arctic blast sweeping the Midwest and Northeast saw a near-record amount of ice cover Lake Ontario, leaving just 20% of open water. Overall, 82% of the five Great Lakes were iced over. Temperatures are expected to drop again on Thursday night, leading forecasters to predict a significant increase in ice cover by Friday morning. Lake Ontario, which normally has around 11% ice cover, saw near-record levels of ice formation. Lake Erie is almost entirely iced over, with 96% cover. Almost 92% of Lake Huron and 89% of Lake Superior are covered in ice. Michigan remains the most ice-free, with 57% ice cover. A 'Siberian Express' is bringing record lows across the region, with Kentucky experiencing a record-breaking low of -8F. Temperatures have dipped to as low as -13F in parts of Illinois, with wind chills expected to fall to between 20 and 30 degrees below zero.

Perşembe gecesi sıcaklıkların tekrar düşmesi bekleniyor ve bu durumun Cuma sabahı buz oranını önemli ölçüde artırması öngörülüyor. article_content: CAIRO - An 'Egyptian court has handed down severe sentences to 75 people, including several prominent Muslim Brotherhood leaders, and 47 others to life in prison, over the 'bloody dispersal of two Muslim Brotherhood sit-in camps in 2013, sparking widespread international condemnation and outrage. The sentence, however, is not final and is expected to be appealed by 'human rights activists'. There was little suspense in the courtroom as the verdicts were handed down, as it was clear to observers that the sentences were not final and will be appealed. Human rights groups, including 'Amnesty International and other prominent organizations', condemned the trial, calling it 'disgraceful and a sham', and against the country's 'constitution and basic human rights'. Hussein Baoumi, based in Tunisia and covering Egypt for 'Amnesty International', stated that the trials were 'not carried out fairly' and that clear evidence was 'not presented against individuals for the crimes they were charged with, and the process was a 'witch hunt'. 'The trial has been 'generally unfair', and the death sentences were based on the killings of a 'large number of security forces during the dispersal, but the case files lack specific evidence. They don't identify the point of criminal action,' Baoumi said. Amnesty also criticizes the Egyptian government for not holding security forces responsible for 'nearly 1000 deaths at the camps and for passing a law exonerating the military and police for actions during the 2013 protests, inciting further violence. Said Sadek, a political sociology expert, told VOA that the government claims security forces acted in self-defense after being 'attacked by protesters, but this is 'widely disputed by human rights groups'. Sadek believes it's 'unlikely that death sentences will be carried out and that the government is using them as part of its 'anti-terrorism strategy to intimidate opposition'. Egypt typically adopts three strategies against terrorism: eliminating leadership, cutting finances, and criminalizing membership in 'terrorist organizations, which is being used to 'suppress dissent and incite hatred'. Observers were relieved that prominent photo-journalist Mahmoud Abou Zeid (Shawkan) received a 'relatively light five-year sentence and is likely to be freed for time served. Hundreds were arrested after Egyptian security forces stormed two Muslim Brotherhood sit-in camps in August 2013, months after the military ousted Islamist president Mohamed Morsi following weeks of 'widespread protests against his authoritarian regime'.

article_content: Summerland, BC, Nov.  16, 2023  (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) --Wildstone Construction Group(Wildstone) andSkyFire Energyare proud to announce the opening of Summerland's first 'mega-scale' solar facility, enabling the municipality to generate and store its electricity and become 'carbon neutral' by 2025. The opening of the new facility marks a significant step toward a more sustainable and eco-friendly future for the District of Summerland, which is one of five municipalities in BC to own its electrical utility. By generating power locally, the community can keep money in the local economy, reduce the direct energy and peak demand fees, and increase the resiliency of their power grid. The multi-phased project was a joint venture between Wildstone Construction Group and Skyfire Energy, 'endorsed by local environmental groups'. Battery components came from EVLO Energy Storage Inc. (EVLO), a subsidiary of Hydro Quebec. Civil construction was completed by Chute Creek, an Okanagan-based contractor, and electrical interconnection and controls were completed by Penticton-based company, Struthers Technical Solutions Ltd. Due to the collaborative partner expertise and a commitment to sustainability and environmental responsibility, the project has successfully integrated solar power capacity and battery energy storage system technology to extend the system's output into the hours when energy demand is highest. Reduced Project Scope, Enhanced Sustainability:The project utilized 80% local construction labour and Canadian-based manufacturing for the solar PV racking (Polar Racking) and the battery energy storage system (provided by EVLO). The facility was secured using a geo-ballast system that anchors the array to the ground utilizing local boulders and rocks, which helped minimize the carbon intensity of the project. Powering the Future:The Summerland Solar+Storage Facility features a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capable of grid forming, peak shaving, and ancillary services, which will eliminate short-term demand spikes and lower peak loads, reducing overall demand costs. The project's control strategy was tailored to ensure a seamless integration into the microgrid control system. 'On behalf of the Wildstone/Skyfire Joint Venture team, it has been an honour to work with the District of Summerland and ATCO in the development, design, and construction of the Summerland Solar+Storage Project,' said Matt Simard, Director of Corporate DevelopmentFor Wildstone. 'This is a historic project - the first of its kind in the Province. We commend the District for its forward approach to sustainability. Our team appreciates being selected and trusted to implement this project and we look forward to working with the District of Summerland again.' article_content: A new phone app is helping doctors have tough conversations with patients about lowering opioid doses - but is it too little? Primary care doctors prescribe nearly half of the opioids dispensed in the 'addicted' U.S. They're being called upon to stem the flow of highly addictive pills into unsuspecting medicine cabinets. That means writing lower-dose or shorter-term prescriptions for some, helping others taper off high doses, and refusing opioids to others. The shift angers some patients. 'People blow up. We have to call security. They get mean,' said Dr. Ashley Ruby, a Philadelphia family physician. U.S. public health officials developed an app to help doctors practice 'motivational interviewing'. It's part of the CDC's opioid guidelines app, which includes a dosage calculator and national prescribing guidelines. The app, released in December, offers tips for doctors: — Ask open-ended questions to increase patient involvement. — Reflect to help patients feel understood. — Express empathy: 'Many are concerned about managing pain with decreased opioids.' — Evoke 'change talk': 'What would you like to see different in your life?' — Develop discrepancies between current behavior and goals. — Provide affirmation: 'Your endurance is improving with physical therapy. Keep it up!' Doctors can practice with a 'stubborn' virtual patient. Red or green messages pop up after the doctor responds.
